newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends lower after cautious session, techs sag.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends lower after cautious session, techs sag.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished lower on Thursday after a cautious session in which shares held to tight trading ranges ahead of the release of a key inflation report on Friday.
The Dow industrials fell 24 points to close unofficially at 6540 as technology and financial issues led the market lower for a second straight session.
"I think we're in a bit of a holding pattern here," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.

With investors awaiting the release of the Producer Price Index (PPI) on Friday, stocks tracked a tentative session in the bond market, where the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury shed 1/32 to yield 7.11 percent in late trading.
Analysts said the cautious atmosphere would likely put a cap on any near-term advances by equities.
"The sentiment is pretty negative here," said Peter Green, director of technical research at Gruntal & Co. "If we do go higher, it's going to be met with selling."
The pessimism was evident in a report that showed new investment in mutual funds fell sharply last month.
According to the Investment Company Institute, new cash flowing to stock mutual funds slowed to an estimated $9.5 billion in March from an $18.45 billion inflow in February.
The mutual fund industry trade group said the March figure was the lowest since July 1996, a month that also brought a significant correction to the stock market.
The mounting pessimism had some analysts wondering if a market bottom was perhaps nearing.
"I think there was an excess of caution over the last couple of weeks," Farley said. Citing technology stocks in particular, she said, "Some of them look very buyable now."

The tech group was among the weakest on Thursday, however, dragging the Nasdaq Composite down by more than one percent. Intel Corp fell five points to 137-1/4, and Microsoft Corp dipped 1-1/4 to 96-3/4.

Among banking shares, which continue to lead the market in its day-to-day gyrations, Citicorp fell 2-3/4 to 110-1/8, Chase Manhattan Corp fell 1-3/8 to 94-1/8, and Wells Fargo and Co slipped 5-1/2 to 270-1/2.
Retailers turned in a mixed performance after reporting their monthly sales figures.
Among the most active issues in the group were Wal-Mart Stores Inc, which fell 1/4 to 28-3/8 and K Mart Corp, which added 1/8 to 12-3/8.
Sears, Roebuck and Co slid 3-7/8 to 47 after announcing it would refund some payments from credit card holders who had filed for bankruptcy. Sears could not say how much it expected to repay.

Microcom Inc, which makes modems and remote-access technologies, surged 5-7/16 to 15-15/16 after agreeing to be acquired by Compaq Computer Corp for 16-1/4 a share, or about $280 million. Shares in Compaq fell 2-3/4 to 75-3/8.
Primark Corp fell 5-1/4 to 18-3/4 after the information technology company warned its first-quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' estimates.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.26 points to 758.34.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 13.66 points to 1235.77.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
